title: Quantization solver perf: 332-arc ILP hangs on Hand-30k
description:
Surfaced during PATCH-67 testing. Our PATCH-42 ILP (ojAlgo branch-and-bound + Gomory cuts) was tested on toy meshes (≤5 arcs / <100ms). At 332 arcs (Hand-30k T-mesh after PATCH-60+68), the solve appears to hang — mvn output stayed empty for 30+ minutes. PATCH-67's end-to-end test currently bypasses with synthetic X[i]=1, getting 39 quads (= 1 quad per Tpatch since X=1 means no subdivision).

Metriko uses a greedy basis-loop heuristic (gen_quantization_basisloop.h ~150 LOC) instead of pure ILP. Their algorithm: compute basis-loop generators of the consistency-constraint kernel, then iteratively shift X by best-scoring generator vector. Faster + scales much better than ILP.

Options:
1. Profile our ILP. Add iteration cap, partial-solution acceptance, or warm start.
2. Port metriko's basis-loop heuristic.
3. Use a hybrid: warm-start ILP with greedy basis-loop solution.

With proper X values (avg ≈3-5 per arc on Hand-30k), each patch subdivides into ~10-25 sub-quads, getting us closer to metriko's 2339 reference.
definition-of-done: Quantization.solve completes in <30s on Hand-30k T-mesh (332 arcs, ~80 4-cycle constraints). PATCH-67 regression with real quantization produces > 500 quads.
testing-plan: 1. Profile current Quantization on T-meshes of size 10/50/100/200/300 to characterize scaling. 2. If ILP doesn't scale, port metriko's basis-loop generator + greedy iterative algorithm. 3. End-to-end run on Hand-30k stage1+2 → quad count comparison vs metriko's 2339.
